experiment: DFM-Fusion Ablation Study: Coverage Check and Per-Entry Truncation
dataset: LoCoMo-10 (1986 QA pairs, 282 multi-hop questions, 10 conversations)

wo_coverage_check.note: 9 out of ~92 fusions per run would have been rejected by the coverage gate (recall < 0.85). Removing the gate allows these merges but the downstream QA impact is small.

wo_per_entry_truncation.note: No queries had the first retrieved item consuming >50% of the budget (B_ret=4000). Memory items are relatively short, so per-entry truncation rarely applies.

key_findings: Neither ablation causes a statistically significant drop in multi-hop F1 (p>0.05)
Both variants show small directional drops (-0.0021 and -0.0023) vs full DFM-Fusion
Full DFM-Fusion significantly outperforms No-Fusion baseline (p=0.031)
Coverage check acts as safety net: 9 fusions would have been rejected, minimal QA impact
Per-entry truncation has no effect when items are short (0% length dominance)
